_note: Alert thresholds for scripts/discord_ops_check.py (H-07). Starting values: the owner confirms or changes them before stage 5c, and they are tuned after the first busy hour. Keys starting with an underscore are notes. Ages and windows are seconds; shares are fractions.
_phase: Given on every run (--phase is required; the function defaults to open, the strictest). pre_open: dark build, no configuration expectations. canary: the tester-only gate (a list of at most canary_max_workspaces); an open gate is an accidental opening. open: after the full opening; the gate must be open and the cap at expected_cap.

severity.page: Act now, inside the confirmed on-call hours: first action from docs/ops/PHONE-RUNBOOK.md within 15 minutes, then tell the owner.
severity.warn: Look in the same working session. Customers may see delays; nothing irreversible is expected, or the condition is expected (a declared burst, an intentional hold).
severity.info: Recorded in the check-in report only.

backlog._split: The lanes' own split (discord.lane.lagging, W-02): a create late above create_warn_seconds warns and above page_lag_seconds pages; a read-back, which a long burst defers, warns only above readback_warn_seconds. Both equal the lane's LAG_WARNING_SECONDS and READBACK_LAG_WARNING_SECONDS (a test pins them). While Discord is paused (execution or authorization off) these rules warn and never page. A projection lag at or below create_warn_seconds (0 when nothing is due) means the newest lagging line is from before a recovery, and it is not read.
backlog._burst: A declared burst (5,000 posts due in one minute) drains in about 21 to 25 minutes at the reviewed 25 requests a second, and one busy workspace can need 20 to 40 minutes (docs/w02/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q6), so the warn level is expected during a burst. The page level (45 minutes) is above the standard's 40-minute maximum with margin and before approvals start lapsing (a post needs re-approval from about 55 minutes after its scheduled time). The real halt detectors are SILENT_HALT_NO_PROGRESS and SILENT_HALT_NO_CREATE.

delivery._upstream: Second review N-9: 5xx answers to creates are deliveries.rejectedUpstream, Discord's side, apart from rejectedSystem (ours: refused for another reason than 403, 404 or 429, uncertain, stuck). DELIVERY_SYSTEM_FAILURES counts them in its attempts but not as failures; DELIVERY_DISCORD_5XX (warn) fires when they exceed server_error_share_warn of at least min_attempts_for_share creates, or when server errors exceed it among the responses of 5 minutes.
delivery._growth: DELIVERY_HELD_GROWTH and DELIVERY_FAILED_GROWTH compare the platform snapshot's publicationHeld and publicationFailed (all platforms, migration 060) with the previous run's report (--previous). The uncertain and stuck-sent warnings also read the unwindowed 'unresolved' counts, so they stay until each admission is reviewed.
delivery._window: Fifteen minutes of the coordinator's publish admissions (one per create attempt). System-caused: 400, 401, 5xx and other non-2xx answers except 403, 404 and 429, transport failures (uncertain), and creates sent but unanswered for two minutes. Customer-caused: 403 (missing permission) and 404 (channel or bot removed).

rate_limit._saturation: Against what the coordinator can admit in a minute: cap x 60 / (window + min(guard, window / 10)), with the guard the serving build reports (config.policy.slotGuardSeconds, SharedPostgresBudget.SLOT_GUARD_SECONDS) or, when a snapshot does not carry it, the largest the coordinator allows.
rate_limit._retention: RATE_RETENTION_BEHIND (limiter B3): the oldest settled row of a kind older than retention_age_factor_warn retentions, retention_remaining_warn settled rows past their retention still present (coordinator.retention.remaining, when the payload carries it), or a purge that could not delete (denied, timeout, error). Fields read when present (proposed to the limiter, not required): coordinator.retention.purged = {status: ok|busy|denied|timeout|error, reads, publications, more, ageSeconds}, the last purge as purge_settled() returns it plus its age; coordinator.retention.remaining = {reads, publications, capped}, settled rows past their retention still present, counted up to a cap through the purge index (capped true when the count stopped there); and the discord.lane.retention log lines (status, reads, publications, more).
rate_limit._invalid: Discord restricts an IP above 10,000 invalid requests in 10 minutes; the policy's own budget is 2,000. Below 25 percent left is ban danger.

cross_tenant._baseline: One denial now and then is a stale tab or an old link. Tune the actor thresholds after a week of baseline lines.

config._expected: expected_lane_flag true or false makes a different lane flag drift; null ignores it. The two expected_* ids are filled in from the release record at each promotion.
